simple.meaning: שְׁדֵמָה (shᵉdêmâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a cultivated field.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across Deuteronomy, 2 Kings, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Habakkuk, beginning at Deuteronomy 32:32. Its contexts include kingship, priesthood, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׁדֵמָה (H7709).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שְׁדֵמָה (shᵉdêmâh) / H7709 is traced through Deuteronomy 32:32, 2 Kings 23:4, Isaiah 16:8, Isaiah 37:27 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: For their vine is of the vine of Sodom,

timeline.evidenceText: For their vine is of the vine of Sodom,

The king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the threshold, to bring out of Yahweh’s temple all the vessels that were made for Baal, for the Asherah, and for all the army of the sky, and he burned them outside of Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron, and carried their ashes to Bethel.

For the fields of Heshbon languish with the vine of Sibmah. The lords of the nations have broken down its choice branches, which reached even to Jazer, which wandered into the wilderness. Its shoots were spread abroad. They passed over the sea.

Therefore their inhabitants had little power. They were dismayed and confounded. They were like the grass of the field, and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like a field before its crop has grown.

The whole valley of the dead bodies and of the ashes, and all the fields to the brook Kidron, to the corner of the horse gate toward the east, will be holy to Yahweh. It will not be plucked up or thrown down any more forever.”
For though the fig tree doesn’t flourish,
